data.narrative:
Vivodyne is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Andrei Georgescu and Dan Huh, having raised $78M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Given data limitations, only the stage-progression method proved applicable. Using total capital raised of $78M as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, this approach yields $156M. The peer-median method was not actionable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting narrow filtering criteria (fewer than 3 datapoints met selection thresholds). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples could not be executed because target revenue remains undisclosed, consistent with private company practice.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $133M to $179M, centered at $156M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x step-up multiplier given Vivodyne's specific capital efficiency and market conditions, as well as the lack of revenue-based anchoring to public biotech multiples (median P/S 6.6x). Additional revenue or profitability data would strengthen conviction in any derived valuation.
